{"id":"persona-qbnm.6","title":"tailscale and oidc cannot answer a challenge; decide what proof means for them","description":"Filed as ONE bead because it is one decision, not two implementations. Splitting follows the decision; it does not precede it.

hire-attestors/src/tailscale.rs reads /localapi/v0/status over tailscaled's Unix socket and returns UserProfile.LoginName. hire-attestors/src/oidc.rs reads cached ID tokens from disk. Both enumerate. Neither can prove, and unlike gpg or did:key that is NOT because the code is missing -- NEITHER HOLDS A KEY THAT CAN ANSWER A CHALLENGE. tailscaled reports what it believes; a cached OIDC token is a bearer artifact sitting in a file.

So Claim::derive's contract bites: evidence must bind to the challenge (Evidence::binds_to), and there is nothing here to bind. Implementing prove() as 'return the thing we read' would manufacture evidence for an identity nothing established, which is precisely the hole the Candidate/Claim split was built to close.

THE REAL QUESTION IS persona-ux32's: what does the daemon need in order to believe an external authority it cannot challenge? Both sources ARE external authorities -- see the external-attestors-are-trusted-by-design memory. Refusing them is not the answer; the whole architecture is built on trusting sources like these. But the trust has to be CALIBRATED and its basis recorded, not implied by the fact that a socket answered.

WHAT MAKES THEM DIFFERENT FROM EACH OTHER, and why the decision may split:
  tailscale  a LIVE authority answering right now over a local socket. Freshness
             is real; the weakness is that tailscaled's word is unverifiable by us.
  oidc       a token AT REST with its own iss/exp and a signature we could
             actually verify against the issuer's JWKS -- which we do not do
             today. That is a cryptographic check we are declining to perform,
             not an impossible one. SPEC-HIRE already grades a non-expired token
             iaa2 and an expired one iaa1.

So oidc may have a real path to verified evidence (fetch the JWKS, check the signature, bind the token to the request some other way), while tailscale may not. Answer that before writing either.","design":"Note this interacts with persona-3tly.1 (presence is hearsay): the general problem of an assertion that cannot be carried to the consumer. A source we cannot challenge is the same defect one layer earlier -- an assertion we cannot verify on arrival.","acceptance_criteria":"A recorded decision for each source on what evidence, if any, it can produce and at what tier; no prove() that returns unverified read-back as evidence.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-09-15T20:50:30.981916543Z","created_by":"agent","updated_at":"2026-09-15T20:50:30.981916543Z","labels":["attestor","driver","security"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"persona-qbnm.6","depends_on_id":"persona-qbnm","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-09-15T20:50:31.013747581Z","created_by":"agent","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"notes":"A THIRD MEMBER OF THIS CLASS, AND IT SPLITS THE CLASS USEFULLY: persona-lbdx, a signed identity attestation on removable media. Like tailscale and oidc it cannot answer a challenge -- a static signed file has nothing to bind to a nonce generated this second.

But it separates two things this bead currently treats as one. tailscale's trust basis is UNVERIFIABLE (tailscaled's word, which nothing here can check) and oidc's is UNVERIFIED (a signature we could check against the issuer's JWKS and do not). lbdx's is VERIFIABLE AND VERIFIED, against a key the user deliberately enrolled per persona-08sz.

So 'cannot answer a challenge' is not one problem. It is two:
  WHOSE WORD IS IT       -- answerable by enrolment and a signature check
  WHEN WAS IT TRUE       -- not answerable by the artifact at all

lbdx answers the first and takes the second from an event the DAEMON observed
(the mount), which is exactly how PlatformIdentity already works: bind by
content match, stamp the instant locally, never let the artifact date itself.

That decomposition is probably the answer for oidc too -- verify the JWKS
signature for the first question, and stop pretending the second is answered by
the token's presence on disk. It is not the answer for tailscale, which fails
the first question and so needs persona-ux32's calibration rather than a
cryptographic check."}
